commits.author: Rui Zhang
commits.message:
[MP][Coordinator] Make the checkpoint the Kafka cursor (#5354)

The Kafka cache-event source (#5286) resumes after a restart from the
consumer group's own committed offset. That offset and the coordinator's
own checkpoint save are independent, on independent timers (offsets
commit roughly every few seconds; a checkpoint every
--checkpoint-interval, default 60s, or only at a clean shutdown). On an
ungraceful crash between two checkpoint saves, the committed offset is
already ahead of what the last saved checkpoint reflects -- and resuming
from it skips the records in between for good: the broker considers them
delivered, and the checkpoint that gets restored does not.

Fix it by having one cursor instead of two. StreamPosition records each
partition's offset as records are admitted and is registered in
checkpoint_components, so save_checkpoint captures it under the same
quiesce as the gate and the views: a checkpoint holds a view and the
exact offset that produced it, and can hold nothing else.
KafkaCacheEventSource's on_assign seeks every assigned partition to
StreamPosition.next_offset(...), which is by construction the right
place for the state just restored. The consumer group no longer commits
at all (enable.auto.commit: False, no store_offsets), so the resume
point moves only when a checkpoint is written. The cost is that
kafka-consumer-groups --describe shows this group no progress; the
position lives in the checkpoint instead.

Nothing needs to measure how far behind a restarting coordinator is,
because there is no window in which its restored view and its resume
point disagree -- it is as consistent as one that has been running for
an hour, just further from the tip. A partition StreamPosition has never
seen (a first start, or one added since) falls back to
auto.offset.reset.

Refs #4226, #4522.

Signed-off-by: Rui Zhang <zrfishnoodles@gmail.com>

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Feature][CB] Per-engine-group scatter head size on CB_REGISTER_ROPE (#5310)

A model may size attention heads per layer type -- Gemma-4 uses 256 on its
sliding layers and 512 on its full-attention ones (global_head_dim) -- so the
single head_size the rope registration carries has no correct value.

Adds an optional group_head_size to CB_REGISTER_ROPE. Empty (the default)
keeps the existing behaviour exactly: head_size covers every group. When
present, _CBRopeState.head_size_for_group resolves the group's own size for
both consumers in the retrieve planner: CBGroupSpec's scatter geometry and
_cb_group_rope_geometry.

Deliberately NOT derived from shape_desc.hs. The fused invariant hs == 2 *
head_size holds for packed K/V, but an MLA latent row is kv_lora_rank +
rope_dim, so hs // 2 would be wrong there. The client knows the real per-layer
head sizes, so it sends them.

group_head_size is distinct from group_rot: the former is scatter geometry,
the latter the rotation window. MLA rotates a narrow slice of a wide latent
row, so the two genuinely differ.

The signature is pinned in four places -- the handler, the protocol payload
classes, the transport ABC, and the ZMQ client -- plus the grpc proto message.
All are updated; missing the transport pair surfaced at runtime as
"cb_register_rope() takes 7 positional arguments but 8 were given".

The server log now reports group_hs so a registration that never reached the
server is distinguishable from one that did.

Verified on gemma-4-E4B: group_map=[0,0,0,0,0,1],
group_rot=[(0,256)x5,(0,512)], group_hs=[256,256,256,256,256,512].

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[CI] fix XPU metadata step failing with PermissionError (#5380)

ci: fix XPU metadata step failing with PermissionError

The "Record XPU runtime metadata" step wrote dist/xpu-runtime.json from
inside the container (which runs as root) into the bind-mounted repo. The
file thus landed on the host owned by root:root, and the subsequent
host-side python3 write_text() -- run as the non-root runner user -- failed
with "PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied", aborting the step
with exit code 1 and skipping the wheel build/smoke-check/upload steps.

Capture the probe output via the host shell's stdout redirect instead, so
the JSON file is created by the runner user. The bind mount is no longer
needed for this step. The torch/vllm import itself was never the problem.

Verified locally against vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v0.26.0: reproduced the
root-owned-file PermissionError, then confirmed the host-redirect variant
produces a runner-owned file and completes successfully.

Signed-off-by: weishu <weishu@tensormesh.ai>

* [feat] Move L2 reconfigure endpoints under the backend-first l2 tier

BREAKING: Move L2 status and operations to /reconfigure/{backend}/l2/*.
The previous unscoped URLs return 404. Preserve the generic backend
contract and strict request schemas; update API/backend documentation
and the existing HTTP route tests.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: jymoon323 <moon960323@gmail.com>

* [feat] Add runtime L1 Device-DAX reconfigure HTTP endpoints

Expose status, add and drain-only remove under /reconfigure/dax/l1
through public StorageManager and L1Manager methods. Keep L1 routes
disjoint from tier-scoped L2 and reuse shared size and error schemas.
Map manager errors through L1ReconfigureError in distributed/error.py.

Preserve primary-arena and live-allocation protections during drain.
Reject runtime L1 additions whose device is already owned by DAX L2,
and interlock multi-arena L1 with adapters that register only one
memory region. Use exact registered paths for L1 removal and leave
device provisioning to operators.

Include HTTP, allocator and portable integration tests and document
the endpoint, error and lifetime contracts.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: jymoon323 <moon960323@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jinyoung Moon <jy323.moon@samsung.com>

* [feat] Publish runtime L1 Device-DAX capacity changes

Derive declared Device-DAX capacity from active arenas and use the
same calculation for local report_status and coordinator capacity
declarations. Publish the existing whole-topology event after runtime
add and drain, including cleanup failures after drain starts.

Resolve the target by its exact registered path when detecting a
failed remove that already changed arena state. Serialize snapshot
construction and enqueue while retaining asynchronous, best-effort
delivery. Include capacity tests and reporting documentation.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: jymoon323 <moon960323@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jinyoung Moon <jy323.moon@samsung.com>

* [fix] Prevent duplicate DAX mappings during runtime add

Check L1 and L2 ownership before DAX hotplug and adapter registration.
Hold the lifecycle lock from the ownership check through mapping to
serialize competing adds, with DAX request handling kept in the adapter
through an ownership callback.

Share physical identity checks for paths and mapped file descriptors.
Detect aliases within L1/L2 and reject duplicate devices in a DAX
config. Return unknown identity on lookup errors and reject
unidentified candidate paths.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: jymoon323 <moon960323@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jinyoung Moon <jy323.moon@samsung.com>

Run L1 add/remove/status and L2 reconfigure/status calls in worker
threads with asyncio.to_thread, including L2 adapter resolution. Await
completion before responding so these blocking calls do not stall other
HTTP requests or coordinator heartbeats.

* [Platform][RBLN] Move MLA block transfer to device-staged _foreach_copy_

Review of #4726 asked for proof that the MLA op sequence (index_select +
stack, .to + index_copy_) does not take torch-rbln's CPU-fallback path on a
real vLLM-RBLN KV cache, and for a comparison against a block-view
_foreach_copy_ implementation.

Traced on DeepSeek-V3 (61 layers, dp8, VLLM_RBLN_USE_DEVICE_TENSOR=1,
torch-rbln 0.4.0rc0 / vllm-rbln 0.11.3a1): neither sequence hits any
torch-rbln bounce site or cpu_fallback, and store->retrieve is byte-exact
for both. The block-view design is adopted anyway:

- no index tensor, so no per-layer read-back of the index to the host
  (index_copy_ cannot take a CPU index, so a gather-side fix alone could
  not cover the scatter);
- every copy is a whole contiguous block, so it takes the direct memcpy_v2v
  path with no submit_or_fallback behind it;
- the L*B block copies of a chunk go through one batched d2d submission
  into a persistent per-thread device staging buffer and the chunk crosses
  the device boundary in one contiguous DMA. On par with the previous
  sequence at one block per chunk; 3.5-5x faster at 2-8 blocks per chunk
  (10-41 ms vs 37-213 ms per chunk on the real KV).

validate_mla_layers now also requires contiguous layers, since a permuted
view would silently send the block copies down the strided path. The
docstrings and README claiming the shared torch path falls to the CPU
fallback via a lazy torch.empty were not reproducible and are replaced by
the measured rationale. Adds a per-thread MLA staging test and a
contiguity test.

commits.author: Yuhan Liu
commits.message:
[Perf][MP] Move LMCache-driven transfer to cudaMemcpyBatchAsync  (#5308)

* [MP][Perf] Move LMCache-driven transfer to cudaMemcpyBatchAsync when eligible

Adds a copy path to the MP server's LMCache-driven STORE/RETRIEVE transfer
that moves each chunk straight between the pinned host object and the engine's
paged KV buffers with one `cudaMemcpyBatchAsync` call per chunk, with no GPU
staging buffer and no scatter kernel. It is taken automatically whenever the
build, the driver and the object group's layout allow it; everything else
keeps using the block transfer kernel.

Motivation: on Kimi-Linear-48B (TP 2, 1024-token MLA pages, 128k prefix) an
nsys A/B shows the kernel path's scatter kernels each waiting ~1.6 ms to be
scheduled on a GPU busy with vLLM's prefill, about 50 ms of stream idle per
128k retrieve while the copies themselves already ran at line rate. The direct
path cut a 128k-token store from 26.6 ms to 19.7 ms per rank on H200.

Changes:
- `csrc/cuda`: `execute_direct_copy_transfer`, `batch_memcpy_supported`,
  `direct_copy_format_supported`, plus `DirectCopyGroupSpec` /
  `DirectCopyObject` descriptors. One `resolve_block_addressing` switch turns
  each eligible `EngineKVFormat` into a base-pointer rule and three byte
  strides (mirroring `calculate_engine_global_offset`, including
  `block_stride_elems` padding); the per-entry loop has no format branches.
  Host ranges are split at `PIN_CHUNK_SIZE` boundaries. Requires CUDA runtime
  and driver >= 12.8; compiled out on HIP.
- `object_group_transfer.py`: `_HAS_BATCH_MEMCPY_ASYNC` resolves build- and
  driver-level support once at import; `direct_transfer_supported` then checks
  the request per object group (host block ids present, no GDS-backed object,
  every kernel group on a token-major layout whose paged block is one
  contiguous run). `transfer_kv_per_object_group` consults both before the
  staged fast path and hands eligible groups to `run_direct_transfer`, which
  mirrors the staged planner's window/skip logic. Ineligible layouts (HND,
  blocked-scale, (K,V)-tuple), GDS objects and older builds fall back to the
  kernel path; an ineligible layout is logged once per format.
- `transfer_kv_per_object_group` takes `block_ids_host`; callers that must
  stay on the kernel path leave it empty, which is how `qstore` keeps its
  current behaviour.
- `BaseCacheContext.get_kernel_group_offset_in_object` and
  `get_kernel_group_kv_pointer_list` (cached on `GPUCacheContext`).
- Torch fallbacks for the two query functions; design doc at
  `docs/design/v1/multiprocess/lmcache_driven_transfer_copy_paths.md`; tip in
  the Kimi Linear recipe.

Tests:
- `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_direct_copy_transfer_gpu.py`: bit-exact parity
  with the kernel path for every eligible format, both directions, skipped
  block prefix, two-group objects, padded MLA stride, pin-boundary splits, and
  rejection of ineligible layouts / out-of-range ids.
- `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_direct_copy_planner_gpu.py`: end to end through
  `transfer_kv_per_object_group` with a real `GPUCacheContext` and
  `LazyMemoryAllocator`, including a Kimi-like 1024-token MLA geometry.
- `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_direct_transfer_dispatch.py`: eligibility and
  dispatch (CPU only).

Signed-off-by: YuhanLiu11 <yliu738@wisc.edu>

* [Test][MP] Capture the direct-copy fallback log independently of LMCACHE_LOG_LEVEL

test_every_kernel_group_must_be_eligible asserted on caplog.records, which
never sees lmcache loggers when LMCACHE_LOG_LEVEL is above INFO: init_logger
sets propagate=False and levels its handlers at LMCACHE_LOG_LEVEL, so the
INFO-level "not eligible" record is filtered before pytest's root handler.
CI runs with WARNING, so the test failed there while passing locally.

Attach a recording handler to the module logger and force its level for the
duration of the test, restoring both afterwards -- the same pattern used in
tests/v1/test_v1_adapter_state_desync.py. Passes with LMCACHE_LOG_LEVEL
unset, DEBUG, WARNING and ERROR.

commits.author: Gawr Gura 0721
commits.message:
[good-first-issue] memory: reject non-positive size in AddressManager (#5115) (#5117)

* memory: reject non-positive size in AddressManager

AddressManager.allocate() and batched_allocate() document that the requested
size must be greater than zero but never checked it, so a zero-byte request
corrupted the explicit free list instead of failing:

* allocate(0) handed out a zero-length block, and freeing it inserted a
  zero-sized entry whose neighbours could never be coalesced again.
  get_free_size() kept reporting the whole heap as free while the next
  full-heap allocation failed with 'no memory is available'.
* batched_allocate(0, n) raised ZeroDivisionError, which TensorMemoryAllocator
  cannot translate into None (it only catches RuntimeError), so the exception
  escaped to LMCacheEngine.store()/store_layer().

Validate size in both methods with the same RuntimeError shape used for
batch_size in #5061, and document it in the Raises sections.

Signed-off-by: Runguo LI <runguo.ai@gmail.com>

* memory: report non-positive allocation size as a caller bug

RuntimeError is overloaded in the allocation stack: every storage backend reads
a failed allocation as memory pressure. Measured with 10 chunks in a
LocalCPUBackend, one zero-byte request evicted all of them with busy_loop=False,
and with busy_loop=True it never returned at all.

Raise ValueError instead, matching the existing ValueError convention for bad
arguments in this allocator API, and stop the engine from ever requesting an
empty chunk: store() and store_layer() now skip degenerate token ranges
(end <= start), which is where the zero-byte request originated.

Signed-off-by: Runguo LI <runguo.ai@gmail.com>

commits.author: Aleksander Pejcic
commits.message:
feat(security): disable /run_script and bind admin HTTP to localhost by default (#5129)

* feat(security): disable /run_script and bind admin HTTP to localhost by default

The admin HTTP surface ships with two insecure defaults:

1. POST /run_script executes caller-supplied Python in-process. The
   restricted builtins are not a security boundary — the injected app
   object alone reaches the whole interpreter object graph — which the
   docs already acknowledge ("treat it as full remote code execution").
   Yet the endpoint is served unconditionally: by the vLLM-embedded
   internal API server whenever internal_api_server_enabled=true, and by
   the standalone lmcache server HTTP frontend, which auto-aggregates
   every internal_api_server/common router (_MP_INCOMPATIBLE_MODULES is
   empty). Neither server authenticates requests.

2. Both servers bind 0.0.0.0 by default (internal_api_server_host and
   --http-host), so the common case exposes the above to the network.

Changes:

- run_script_api_enabled (LMCACHE_RUN_SCRIPT_API_ENABLED), default
  false: /run_script returns 404 unless explicitly enabled.
- lmcache server: --run-script-api-enabled flag (default false) wired
  into MPServerConfig.
- internal_api_server_host and --http-host now default to 127.0.0.1.

Operators who use /run_script set one flag; multi-node admin access
sets the bind host explicitly. Docs (common_apis, mp/http_api,
mp/configuration, api_reference/configurations) and the run_script
test suites are updated to match.

commits.author: Rui Zhang
commits.message:
[MP] Isolate a failing cache-event consumer from the others (#5465)

CacheEventBroadcaster called its consumers in a plain loop. A consumer
that raised stopped the loop, so every consumer registered after it
missed the batch, while the gate had already admitted it and would drop
a resend as a duplicate. One buggy controller could leave the key
directory or the usage view behind.

broadcast and fence_instance now catch each consumer's exception, log
it with the batch's instance, incarnation and seq, and go on to the
next consumer. Only the
consumer that raised misses the batch.

The batch is not retried. Consumers only touch memory, so the same
batch would fail the same way, and re-sending it to every consumer
would apply it twice to the ones that succeeded.

Signed-off-by: Rui Zhang <zrfishnoodles@gmail.com>

commits.author: Rui Zhang
commits.message:
[MP] Let the Kafka producer buffer and retry cache events (#5464)

KafkaCacheEventSink.publish produced each batch and then flushed,
blocking the bus drain thread until the broker acknowledged or
delivery_timeout (10 s by default) ran out. Anything not acknowledged
in time raised, and the subscriber dropped the whole flush. A broker
restart longer than 10 s therefore became a permanent sequence gap,
although the idempotent producer could have retried it in order.

publish now follows the usual Kafka producer pattern. It hands records
to the producer's buffer, serves earlier delivery reports with poll(0),
and returns without waiting. Only close() flushes, for at most 10 s.
The producer retries in order for up to delivery_timeout, now 300 s by
default, so a broker restart delays events instead of losing them.
The producer's buffer is capped at 64 MB.

A record that does not fit the buffer, or that the producer gives up
on, is dropped and counted in dropped_batches. Its seq is already
spent, so the coordinator sees the gap. A full buffer still raises
CacheEventPublishError, so the subscriber restores a capacity
declaration as before. A declaration the producer drops later is not
re-sent; that is documented as a known limitation.

The HTTP transport is unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Rui Zhang <zrfishnoodles@gmail.com>

commits.author: Rui Zhang
commits.message:
[MP] Test real MP servers against the coordinator end to end (#5519)

Starts `lmcache server` processes, CPU-only, against a coordinator on a
thread, and checks both the batches each server sent, read from its own
events trace, and what the coordinator's directory made of them.

- MP-1: a store is one STORE batch per backend (L1, node-local L2,
  shared L2) with tier, backend, shared flag, size, tokens and offset.
- MP-2: a delete through the server's API is a DELETE for that tier and
  backend alone; chunks evicted from a full L1 come back as L1 DELETEs
  and the directory follows.
- MP-3: every compartment's capacity is declared under one revision on
  registering, and again under the next revision on registering again.
- MP-4: a restart reports under a higher incarnation, sequence back at
  1, without re-reporting; the coordinator fences L1 and keeps L2.
- MP-5: batches published while the Kafka broker is down are held by
  the producer and delivered once it is back, in order with the same
  sequence numbers, and the coordinator ends with every store. This one
  runs in-process on the fake broker, so it is an ordinary unit test.
- MP-6: a coordinator delete by token ids reaches the server and its
  DELETEs empty the directory.
- MP-7: a prefetch through the coordinator loads L2 back into L1, and
  its status, read through the coordinator, finds every key.

mp_server_harness.py holds the pieces: the coordinator thread, the
server subprocess, and a KV client that stores through the transfer
context over POSIX shared memory, as `lmcache bench server --mode cpu`
does.

The tests start subprocesses, so unit runs skip them unless RUN_MP_E2E=1.
The coordinator integration pipeline (.buildkite/coordinator_controllers/)
sets it and runs them, CPU-only, before the coordinator-controllers suite;
the step fails if either does.
The controllers suite now runs with RUN_E2E=1 too, so its own end-to-end
tests, real MP servers with its controllers loaded, run there as well.

Signed-off-by: Rui Zhang <zrfishnoodles@gmail.com>

commits.author: Dongjoo Seo
commits.message:
[1/N][Refactor][MP] Add ordered L1 write overflow and object owner tags (#5416)

* feat(mp): support multiple L1 managers

Add tagged DRAM and GDS configurations through repeatable --l1-manager
JSON arguments, retaining legacy DRAM options and moving GDS configuration
to the new interface.

Route writes through a placement policy, give each L1 its own eviction
and store controllers, and bind L2 adapters to L1 affinity tags. Look up
peer L1s concurrently and preserve read ownership across overlapping
prefetches. Report per-L1 status and metrics and aggregate capacity by
backing medium. Keep the existing single-GDS-slab process limit explicit.

Add coverage for configuration validation, placement, concurrent lookups,
failed-lookup cleanup, overlapping reads, adapter lifecycle, and reporting.
Validation: 406-test regression suite, 93 follow-up checks, and 98 tests
after the concurrent-lookup change passed. Applicable pre-commit checks
passed; Rust hooks were skipped for this Python-only change.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* docs(mp): document multi-L1 configuration and migration

Add a user-facing guide for tagged L1 managers, per-manager settings, L2 affinity, write and prefetch behavior, GDS migration, reporting, and transport limits. Update existing MP references to the new configuration interface.

Validate all five guide commands with the configuration parser and check the rendered HTML and local links. Documentation pre-commit checks pass. The strict Sphinx build reproduces the same 36 diagnostics as the committed baseline, with none introduced by these changes.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* test(mp): update L1 configuration fixtures for tagged managers

Give the DevDax compatibility test doubles the default L2 affinity tag so they reach the single-region validation instead of raising AttributeError. Preserve the NIXL and Mooncake RDMA rejection checks and the Mooncake TCP acceptance check.

Migrate remaining GDS discovery tests to --l1-manager JSON. Cover separate DevDax and GDS managers while retaining rejection of both backends within one manager.

Validation: 52 DevDax/GDS tests and 14 multi-L1 configuration tests passed. Applicable pre-commit checks passed.
Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [MP] Narrow multi-L1 to write overflow and object owner tags

Keep synchronous, ordered OUT_OF_MEMORY overflow at existing batch granularity. Stamp a process-local MemoryObj owner at L1 allocation and route completion using captured owner/key groups through the existing MessagePack callback dispatcher. Reset the tag for recycled paged objects.

Preserve single-L1 production configuration and legacy GDS flags. Restrict internal multi-manager construction to write-only tests with no L2 or eviction. Defer JSON configuration, affinity, parallel lookup, owner side tables, and per-manager reporting.

Validation: 251 focused tests, 47 standalone engine-transfer tests, and 10 real GPU tests passed. Applicable pre-commit checks and focused Sphinx passed; full Sphinx reproduces 31 unchanged merge-base diagnostics.
Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Fix][MP] Preserve single-L1 completion trace replay

Record the existing key-only finish_write trace once for both completion entry points. Keep process-local owner identities in native callback routing, not persistent storage traces. Leave the trace schema and replay dispatcher unchanged.

Add regressions covering legacy and owner-routed completion, MessagePack trace arguments, and replay into a fresh L1 manager. Both cases reproduced the unsupported or duplicated trace entries before the fix.

Validation: 432 compatibility and trace tests, 47 standalone engine-transfer tests, and 10 real GPU tests passed. Applicable pre-commit checks and focused Sphinx passed.
Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* perf(mp): validate L1 write policy at construction

Capture and validate the candidate order once for the fixed manager set.
Reserve writes through the resolved manager tuple, removing policy calls,
set creation, and registry checks from the write path. Later mutations of
the supplied policy no longer reconfigure the storage manager.

Update the constructor validation and snapshot tests and document the
fixed-order contract.

Addresses: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/5416#discussion_r4161736468
Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* fix(mp): handle write completion preparation failures

Prepare the owner/key payload inside the existing store failure boundary
before marking the store successful. An ownership validation error now
reports a failed store and still publishes MP_STORE_END with zero counts.
Retain staging buffers under the existing write-TTL rules because queued
GPU copies may still reference them.

Cover invalid ownership with one and two managers, verify failure events
and absence of completion callbacks, and document the cleanup behavior.

Addresses: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/5416#discussion_r4161833495
Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* fix(mp): guard single-L1 reporting in the overflow harness

Require one L1 for memcheck, get_l1_usage, report_status, and capacity publication. The internal multi-manager harness is write-only and must not report partial health or capacity from its primary manager.

Preserve single-L1 reporting, document the limitation, and extend the public-interface rejection and compatibility checks. Validation: 107 tests and applicable pre-commit checks passed. The Sphinx build retains the same 31 baseline diagnostics.

commits.author: Dongjoo Seo
commits.message:
[3/N][Refactor][MP] Add L1ManagerInterface (#5528)

* [Fix][CUDA] Clear the pending error after a failed host (un)register

cudaHostRegister can fail, for example on a file-backed mapping of a
disk filesystem, and the Device-DAX allocators then fall back to
pageable copies. The CUDA runtime kept that failure pending in the
calling thread, and torch raised it as "CUDA error: invalid argument"
at the thread's next kernel launch, long after the fallback had been
taken.

Read the error back with cudaGetLastError whenever cudaHostRegister or
cudaHostUnregister returns a non-zero status, through the runtime
library torch already loaded, so a handled failure stays handled.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [3/N][Refactor][MP] Add L1ManagerInterface

StorageManager, the storage controllers and the serde wrapper were typed
against the concrete L1Manager. Add L1ManagerInterface to
internal_api.py, a runtime-checkable Protocol of exactly the calls they
make, and type them against it; L1Manager satisfies it unchanged. Make
the id counter and read-lock clamp of l1_manager.py public so every
implementation shares them. StorageManager.l1_memory_desc now raises
instead of returning None for an L1 without a registerable buffer,
which the interface's "L1MemoryDesc | None" return made explicit.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[cb] Best-effort whole-chunk L2 loading: whole-column staging + partial-chunk handling (#5434)

* [Bugfix][Blend] A partially loaded chunk is not stale: no strike, release its locks

The sparse leg's prefetch is best-effort: under L1 pressure the prefetch
controller loads what fits, so a chunk can come back with some of its
(read group x rank) keys loaded and the rest not. _sparse_classify
already (correctly) refuses to blend such a chunk, but it then handled
it as if the chunk were gone from storage:

1. It took a stale strike, and at 2 strikes the chunk was removed from
   the fingerprint index permanently -- for content that is still stored
   and merely did not fit L1 at that moment. Under sustained L1 pressure
   this guts the index and the blend hit rate never recovers.

2. Its loaded keys stayed read-locked for the read TTL (300 s default).
   Only found chunks are stashed for the retrieve/release path, so a
   partial chunk's landed rows were locked for a caller that can never
   use them, deepening the very L1 pressure that caused the shortfall.

Classify such chunks as partial: no strike (the strike path is kept for
chunks with NO rows loaded -- those are genuinely gone), and release the
landed keys' whole reservation immediately.

Blend-module only; the prefetch controller and "full"-policy semantics
are unchanged (other "full" callers -- warm prefetch, P2P -- legitimately
consume per-row gaps).

Measured on GLM-5.2-FP8 TP8, 750-permutation blend workload, 100 GB L1 +
fs_native L2, where reservation shortfalls made partial chunks routine.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Feat]  support for Re-RoPE   KV caches (per-tensor e4m3/e5m2) (#5500)

* [Feat][Blend] Re-RoPE fp8 KV caches (per-tensor e4m3/e5m2)

vLLM allocates --kv-cache-dtype fp8 KV as uint8, which the retrieve-plan
builder could not map to a rope scalar type: every plan came back None,
so every fp8 request raised "native plan unavailable" and degraded to
full recompute. The blend did nothing while still paying its overhead.

The fix threads the fp8 flavor end to end:

- CB_REGISTER_ROPE gains a trailing, defaulted kv_quant payload
  ("fp8_e4m3" / "fp8_e5m2"; "" keeps today's behavior) stored on
  _CBRopeState. The buffer dtype alone cannot name the bit layout.
- The plan builder resolves uint8 K planes through the declared flavor
  (and true float8 torch dtypes directly), and passes the cos/sin
  cache's own scalar type: under fp8 KV the cache stays in the model's
  float dtype, so CBGroupSpec now carries cache_scalar_type (defaulted
  to key_scalar_type for older planners).
- The fused ramp rope kernel is templated on key and cache types and
  dequantizes -> rotates -> requantizes fp8 keys. No scale is involved:
  rotation commutes with the per-tensor scale, which is identical on
  input and output. Homogeneous instantiations keep their exact
  pre-change numerics (the conversion helper is the identity there).

Scope: legacy-geometry (standard attention) models. Under a declared
rope map, rot_for_group still skips non-float kernel groups — a
quantized index side-plane and quantized main KV are indistinguishable
by dtype there, so fp8 MLA/GLM stays out of scope.

Tested: dequant-rotate-requant parity against a per-op bf16-rounded
reference through execute_cb_retrieve_plan_flat on H200, scalar-type
resolution units, and the existing rope/plan/retrieve/store suites.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Review] Inline the key-scalar resolution; one-line kv_quant docs

Review follow-ups on #5500: fold _cb_key_at_scalar into its only call
site in the plan builder, pin the flavor maps in the test instead, and
cut the kv_quant field/arg comments to one line.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Review] Reuse the dispatch machinery; drop the speculative float8 map

Minimize per review: the fused-rope launcher nests an
LMC_DISPATCH_ROPE_KEY_TYPES switch (floating + fp8 cases) instead of a
hand-rolled helper and if-chain; the true-float8-dtype map goes (vLLM
allocates fp8 KV as uint8 — no caller); kv_quant validation keys off
_FP8_FLAVOR_TO_AT_SCALAR instead of a literal.

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Bugfix][KV format] Detect the rank-4 DSA indexer cache as NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS (#5562)

vLLM >= 0.29 drops the indexer backend's own (num_blocks, block_size, 132)
shape and allocates the fp8 indexer cache through the MLA spec with a
singleton head axis, [NB, BS, 1, 132]. The vLLM detector's rank-4 rule
(fused K/V rows) ran first, so the blocked [BS x vals | BS x scales] page
layout was copied as 132-byte token rows: exact only while a token keeps
its block offset, scrambled for any CacheBlend hit shifted off the block
grid (GLM-5.2: recall 0.0 at 16k, correct at a 64-aligned shift).

Squeeze the singleton head axis of a uint8 width-132 plane before the
rank-4 rule so it reaches NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS as the rank-3 cache does.

Signed-off-by: weishu <weishu@tensormesh.ai>

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[CI] Fix XPU smoke-check quoting and RC image tag validation (#5609)

Two release-workflow bugs blocked artifact publication for 0.5.6rc4.

1. The XPU wheel smoke check embedded `{', '.join(missing)}` inside a
   single-quoted `bash -lc '...'` block. The literal `'` terminated that
   quoted word, unbalancing the remaining `\"` escapes, so the container
   shell aborted with "unexpected EOF while looking for matching" before
   running the check. Formatting the list directly avoids the inner
   quotes entirely. Present since #4616, so the check has never actually
   run; it failed identically on v0.5.6rc1..rc3.

2. The RC image job's tag check was the bare `[[ ]] && ...` as the last
   command of a `set -e` step, so a non-matching tag killed the job with
   no diagnostic at all. 0.5.6rc4 was tagged without the `v` prefix every
   prior release carried, so it failed there and no RC image was pushed.

   The `v` is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: setuptools-scm only

   labeled with the previous release. Keep requiring it and emit an
   explicit ::error:: naming the offending tag, so the mis-tag is

commits.author: seungrokj
commits.message:
[Perf][MP][ROCm] Enable the direct copy-engine transfer on ROCm/HIP (#5358)

* [Perf][MP][ROCm] Enable the direct copy-engine transfer on ROCm/HIP

PR #5308 gated the LMCache-driven direct copy-engine transfer to CUDA on the
premise that cudaMemcpyBatchAsync has no HIP equivalent. ROCm 7.x (HIP 7.15)
ships hipMemcpyBatchAsync with the identical 9-arg (failIdx) signature, plus
hipMemcpyAttributes and hipMemcpySrcAccessOrderStream, so the same path works
once the sources are hipified.

- csrc/cuda/mp_mem_kernels.cu: enable LMC_HAS_BATCH_MEMCPY under
  USE_ROCM && HIP_VERSION >= 71500000; include <hip/hip_version.h>; on ROCm
  skip the CUDA-versioned (>= 12080) runtime/driver check in
  batch_memcpy_supported() since the compile-time guard already ensures the API.
- setup_extensions/build_profiles/rocm.py: torch's bundled hipify map predates
  the batched-copy API, so patch the hipified output for the tokens it misses
  (cudaMemcpyBatchAsync, cudaMemcpyAttributes, cudaMemcpySrcAccessOrderStream,
  cudaStreamPerThread).
- Docs and GPU-test skip reasons updated for the ROCm path.

Isolated to ROCm: under a CUDA build (USE_ROCM undefined) the preprocessed
source is byte-identical to before, and LMC_HAS_BATCH_MEMCPY still resolves to
1 on CUDA >= 12.8. Verified on MI355X (gfx950): cuda_ops builds for all arches,
batch_memcpy_supported() is True, direct-copy GPU parity tests pass (29 passed;
full suite 53 passed / 2 skipped).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: seungrokj <seungrok.jung@amd.com>

* [ROCm] Gate direct copy-engine path behind opt-in env var

batch_memcpy_supported() on ROCm previously returned true whenever the
HIP >= 7.15 compile guard passed, but that guard cannot prove the op is
functional: some HIP builds link hipMemcpyBatchAsync yet return
hipErrorNotSupported at runtime (observed on ROCm 7.2.3, where the symbol
exists but the batched copy is a stub). Make the ROCm direct copy-engine
path opt-in -- it is enabled only when LMCACHE_ROCM_ENABLE_BATCH_MEMCPY is
set to a non-zero value, otherwise the connector falls back to the staging
kernel. CUDA behaviour is unchanged.

Signed-off-by: seungrokj <seungrok.jung@amd.com>

* [ROCm] Require device-addressable host pointers for the direct copy path

hipMemcpyBatchAsync's copy engine dereferences the host operand directly, so
the hipHostRegister'd pinned host pool must be device-addressable. On configs
where hipDeviceAttributeCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem == 0 (observed on
MI300/MI355 ROCm builds) a registered host VA is not device-usable, and the
batched D2H/H2D copy faults asynchronously with a GPU memory access fault
(hipHostGetDevicePointer returns the same, still-unusable VA, so translation
does not help). The legacy hipMemcpyAsync kernel path tolerates such memory,
which is why only the copy-engine path faulted.

Gate batch_memcpy_supported() on the attribute in addition to the opt-in env
var, so the connector transparently falls back to the staging kernel where the
copy engine cannot address the registered host pool.

Signed-off-by: seungrokj <seungrok.jung@amd.com>

* [ROCm] Add LMCACHE_ROCM_FORCE_BATCH_MEMCPY to skip the host-pointer attribute check

Some ROCm builds report hipDeviceAttributeCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem
as 0 even though the hipHostRegister'd host VA is device-addressable
(MI355X, ROCm 10 / HIP 7.15). There, batch_memcpy_supported() returns
False even with LMCACHE_ROCM_ENABLE_BATCH_MEMCPY=1, so the direct
copy-engine path is never used although the batched copy works.

Keep the attribute check as the default, but let an explicit
LMCACHE_ROCM_FORCE_BATCH_MEMCPY (non-zero, together with
LMCACHE_ROCM_ENABLE_BATCH_MEMCPY) skip it once the parity tests pass.
Document it next to the existing opt-in.

Validated on 8x MI355X (gfx950), torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0:
- ENABLE only: batch_memcpy_supported() == False, direct-copy tests skip.
- ENABLE + FORCE: True; test_direct_copy_transfer_gpu.py and
  test_direct_copy_planner_gpu.py 29/29 pass.
- FORCE alone: False (still requires the opt-in).
- tests/v1/multiprocess + tests/v1/platform with ENABLE + FORCE:
  1172 passed, 61 skipped, 0 failed.

Suggested-by: hyukjlee
Signed-off-by: seungrokj <seungrok.jung@amd.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [MP] Update direct-transfer comment for HIP support

The _HAS_BATCH_MEMCPY_ASYNC comment still said the direct copy-engine
path is built against CUDA >= 12.8, not HIP. It is now also built
against HIP >= 7.15 (hipMemcpyBatchAsync), gated at runtime by
LMCACHE_ROCM_ENABLE_BATCH_MEMCPY.

Signed-off-by: seungrokj <seungrok.jung@amd.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Charlie Fu
commits.message:
[Bugfix] Keep vLLM's device in CreateGPUConnector under data parallelism (#5501)

* [Bugfix] Keep vLLM's device in CreateGPUConnector under data parallelism

Each vLLM data-parallel rank is its own engine whose TP/PP world starts
at rank 0, so metadata.local_worker_id is 0 on every data-parallel rank.
With --data-parallel-size-local > 1, CreateGPUConnector called
set_device(0) on every rank and moved DP rank >= 1 onto rank 0's GPU,
while its weights and KV cache stayed on its own GPU.

vLLM binds each worker to its device in Worker.init_device before the KV
connector is created, so use the current device on the vLLM path.

Signed-off-by: charlifu <charlifu@amd.com>

* [Bugfix] Offset vLLM local_worker_id by the data-parallel rank

Each vLLM data-parallel rank is its own engine whose TP/PCP/PP world
starts at rank 0, so calculate_local_rank_and_world_size() returned
local_worker_id 0 on every data-parallel rank. CreateGPUConnector then
called set_device(0), moving data-parallel rank 1 off the device vLLM
bound it to. Later kernels (e.g. Triton, which launches on the current
device's stream) ran on a different GPU than vLLM's work, which caused
"Memory access fault by GPU" with data parallelism + expert parallelism
under CUDA/HIP graphs.

Compute the device index the way vLLM's Worker.init_device does: offset
by the local data-parallel rank times the per-engine world size (except
for the ray / external_launcher backends, a ray data-parallel backend,
or multi-node-per-DP setups, where vLLM does not offset), then map it
through current_platform.logical_device_id_to_visible_device_id.

This replaces the previous approach of using torch_dev.current_device()
in CreateGPUConnector, so LMCache no longer relies on the caller having
set the device, and local_worker_id is correct for other users (e.g. the
NIXL storage backend's endpoint selection).

Signed-off-by: charlifu <charlifu@amd.com>

commits.author: Hyukjoon Lee
commits.message:
[Fix][MP] Fail closed in free_lookup_locks; add --session-ttl-seconds (#5457)

free_lookup_locks rebuilds the lock set from the session's recorded
prefetch hit length. When none is recorded (the session was reaped while
the request sat in the engine queue, or the result was never consumed)
it still released the whole [start, end) range for full-attention groups.
That range can extend past what the prefetch locked, and object keys are
shared across requests, so it stripped concurrent readers' read locks:
their RETRIEVE then failed with KEY_NOT_READABLE, which the vLLM connector
reports as invalid_block_ids -- fatal for hybrid models with several KV
cache groups. Seen on Kimi-K3 (MLA + KDA), TP 8 / DCP 8, 8x MI355X under
a 70-concurrency agentic trace: ~1000 "finish read on non-read-locked key"
warnings, then EngineCore death ~25 min in. Release nothing in that case
and leave held locks to the L1 read TTL, as sliding-window groups already
did.

Session reaping is what loses the hit length. Requests can wait in vLLM's
queue for longer than the hard-coded 600 s session TTL, so expose it as
--session-ttl-seconds (default unchanged). #4091 proposed the flag and was
closed for lack of a concrete scenario; this is one.

Also document the ROCm 10 / MI355X settings for Kimi-K3 (rocm7.2 wheel on
ROCm 10, DCP 8 chunk size, eager L1 pinning, read/session TTLs).

commits.author: zhongerdeajie
commits.message:
[Bugfix][Test] Stabilize the extra_stats throughput test with wall-clock timestamps (#5612)

* test(mp_observability): anchor extra_stats throughput timestamps to wall clock

Fixes #4566

The two extra_stats throughput tests inject events with fabricated
absolute timestamps (100.0 / 200.0). The subscriber prunes pending
STARTs older than _PENDING_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (60s) against time.time()
(_prune_pending), so those timestamps are always stale. _maybe_flush
runs on every event; when a CI runner takes longer than the flush
interval between dispatching START and END, that flush prunes the
just-registered pending START, the END no longer correlates, and the
logged throughput degrades to avg_copy=n/a, failing the assertion.
